A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MV-MATH benchmark and include the main text and Appendices A–H. Text and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison, including the image-heavy appendices.

before.justification: V5 reports original model evaluations, human performance, prompting and image-input comparisons, and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V6 retains the original empirical evaluations and human results, and adds three qualitative model-error examples in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, filtering, annotation, and model-evaluation procedures are retained. No algorithm, model architecture, objective, or inference component is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: Both report 2,009 K-12 problems across the same 11 subjects, three difficulty levels, and question formats. The added appendix examples remain within existing geometry coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–4, Tables 10–14, and Figure 4, including the model variants and human comparison. The additional error cases continue to examine Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

E3.justification: The 200-question testmini set, 50-student human evaluation, prompting conditions, image-input comparisons, SAR/QCR metrics, and Appendix B generation settings are unchanged. The added case illustrations document no new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds three Claude failure cases: cube unfolding, volume reconstruction from multiple views, and refusal on a cylindrical-block problem (v6 Figures 22, 24, and 29). Existing prompting analyses, input comparisons, and the 100-error distribution are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-performance confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run/seed counts. V6 introduces no change to uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Scores in Tables 2–4 and 10–14 and existing plots are unchanged. V6 adds three qualitative response entries, including Claude's volume answer of 5 against ground truth 8 in Figure 24. Figure 1 also changes the knight-move example answer from 18 to 12 while retaining the stated 25 × 25 problem.

T1.justification: The coefficient-of-variation formula, SAR/QCR definitions, and difficulty-grading assumptions are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or formal derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about the human–model gap, image dependence, sequential input, and inconsistent benefits from CoT prompting.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning visual perception, cross-image dependencies, prompting, and training-related generalization are retained. The new examples illustrate the existing error taxonomy without adding substantive mechanisms, applicability boundaries, or limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 removes 'Zujuan' as the named source of approximately 380,000 crawled questions, reducing provenance disclosure without documenting an actual source change. Hardware, generation settings, prompts, model links, and the data/code access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. References for CMMaTH, MATH-Vision, and MathVerse receive publication-record updates; these represent the same works rather than additions to related work.

P1.justification: V6 makes limited copyedits and prose shortening, updates bibliographic metadata, and adds a funding acknowledgment. The main-section sequence and Appendix A–H organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is restyled, three Appendix H figures are added, and subsequent cases are renumbered. The final page now contains two refusal examples. Captions and text flow receive limited adjustments, and printed page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: The additional error examples offer modest illustrative value, but v6 introduces an incorrect answer in Figure 1: 18 becomes 12, although 12 knight moves cannot reach opposite corners of the stated 25 × 25 grid. Removing the named data source in Appendix F.1 also reduces traceability. These losses outweigh the limited illustrative and editorial gains; the unchanged core evaluations keep the deterioration limited.
